mainTopic: Who counts as a יחיד for private fasts, rules for keeping a fast, and travel advice drawn from יעקב and יוסף
overview: The amud opens with the last line of a list from the previous discussion: days written in מגילת תענית. A ברייתא then teaches that every תלמיד חכם counts as a יחיד for the private fasts. It also defines a יחיד and a תלמיד. Two more ברייתות record a debate about whether anyone may take on these roles by himself. The answer given is that painful practices like fasting may be taken on, and the person is remembered for good. Next come rules for keeping a fast: you finish a fast once you start it, and a traveller follows the stricter place. Someone who ate by mistake should not look full in public, as יעקב warned his sons. The גמרא then turns to יוסף's travel advice to his brothers. Review Torah on the road but do not analyze deeply. Do not take long strides. Travel only in daylight. Finally, רבי חייא says a traveller should eat little, and the גמרא gives two reasons and starts explaining how they differ, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Days written in מגילת תענית
steps.stepSummary: The last item of a list from the earlier discussion: the holidays recorded in מגילת תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And on the festive days that are written in מגילת תענית.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a list that began before this section. It adds the special days written in מגילת תענית to the days when fasting is not done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מגילת תענית is an ancient list of happy dates when the חכמים did not allow fasting. Adding it here means those days are also left out when fasts are held.

keyTerms.meaning: An ancient list of dates on which fasting was not allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מגילת תענית (a list of days when you may NOT fast) with מסכת תענית, the tractate you are learning now.

phrases.english: And on the festive days that are written in Megillat Taanit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְיָמִים טוֹבִים הַכְּתוּבִין בִּמְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list from the previous discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The days listed in מגילת תענית are also excluded from fasting.

steps.title: Every תלמיד חכם counts as a יחיד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person should not avoid the יחיד fasts by saying he is only a תלמיד, because all תלמידי חכמים are יחידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person should not say, 'I am only a student, I am not fit to be a יחיד.' Rather, all Torah scholars are יחידים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא begins. It tells a learner not to excuse himself from the private fasts by saying he is too small to count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the יחידים begin fasting when rain is late. A modest scholar might think that word only means great people. The ברייתא says every תלמיד חכם is included, so he too should fast.

keyTerms.meaning: An outstanding individual who fasts privately for rain

steps.whyThisMatters: It widens the group of people expected to fast, so humility does not become a reason to skip it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person should not say, 'I am a student,'
'I am not fit to be a yachid.'
phrases.notes: He is thinking of the יחידים in the משנה who start fasting when the rain is late.

phrases.english: Rather, all Torah scholars are yechidim.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַל יֹאמַר אָדָם תַּלְמִיד אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about who counts as a יחיד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All תלמידי חכמים count as יחידים for the private fasts.

steps.title: Asking for definitions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what exactly a יחיד is and what a תלמיד is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is a יחיד and who is a תלמיד?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא stops to ask for clear definitions of the two words it just used. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used both titles. Now it wants to know where the line between them is.

phrases.english: Who is a yachid and who is a student?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ יָחִיד וְאֵיזֶהוּ תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define the terms used in step 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact definitions of a יחיד and a תלמיד

steps.title: Defining יחיד and תלמיד
steps.stepSummary: A יחיד is someone fit to lead the community. A תלמיד is someone who can answer a question of הלכה in what he learns, even in the tractate studied that season.
steps.simpleTranslation: A יחיד is anyone fit to be appointed leader over the community. A תלמיד is anyone who is asked a matter of הלכה in his learning and answers it, even in the tractate of the כלה gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question by giving a clear test for each title.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יחיד is a higher level: someone a community could appoint as its leader. A תלמיד only needs to answer correctly in the area he studies. Even the single tractate everyone studied that season is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A leader appointed over the community
The tractate studied in the כלה gathering months

steps.whatToRemember: יחיד = fit to lead the community. תלמיד = can answer a question of הלכה in his own learning, even if only in the season's tractate.

phrases.aramaic: יָחִיד — כֹּל שֶׁרָאוּי לְמַנּוֹתוֹ פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּבּוּר,
phrases.english: A yachid is anyone fit to be appointed leader over the community;
a student is anyone whom they ask
a matter of halacha in his learning, and he answers,
and even in the tractate of the kallah.
phrases.notes: This means the tractate the whole community studied together that season, at the כלה gatherings.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָחִיד — כֹּל שֶׁרָאוּי לְמַנּוֹתוֹ פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יחיד = fit to lead the community; תלמיד = can answer a question of הלכה in his studies, even in the season's tractate

steps.title: רבי מאיר: not everyone may take on these roles
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: according to רבי מאיר, not everyone who wants to may act as a יחיד or a תלמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Not everyone who wants to make himself a יחיד may do so, nor may everyone make himself a תלמיד. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא asks whether a person may choose on his own to act like a יחיד or a תלמיד, for example by fasting like them. רבי מאיר says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's concern is that someone who is not truly on that level may not simply take on the title or its practices by himself. The next step brings רבי יוסי, who disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: To make himself (to act as if he were)
These are the words of רבי מאיר

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כׇּל הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת עַצְמוֹ יָחִיד עוֹשֶׂה,
phrases.english: Not everyone who wants to make himself a yachid may do so;
[nor may everyone make himself] a student;
phrases.notes: Literally this says 'a student — does.' Here it's read as carrying over 'not everyone' from the line before, though it can also mean a real student may take this on.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כׇּל הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת עַצְמוֹ יָחִיד עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the titles to whether one may take them on by himself
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a person may not decide on his own to act as a יחיד or a תלמיד.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: he may, since it brings pain, not praise
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says a person may take on the role and is remembered for good, because fasting brings him pain, not honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: He may do so, and he is remembered for good, because it is not praise for him but pain for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with רבי מאיר and allows anyone to take on these practices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason: taking on fasts is not a way of showing off. It only brings suffering. Since it is not about honor, there is no problem of acting above one's level.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: He may do so,
and he is remembered for good,
because it is not praise for him,
but rather it is pain for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may take on the fasting practices of a יחיד or תלמיד, since they bring pain, not praise.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says not everyone may
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא gives the same strict view, this time in the name of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: Not everyone who wants to make himself a יחיד may do so, nor may everyone make himself a תלמיד. These are the words of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same debate. Here the strict view has a different author. It sets up a new way of explaining the other side in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as רבי מאיר's in step 5, but this ברייתא is a separate source with a different author. Its other side, in the next step, sets up a new distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כׇּל הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת עַצְמוֹ יָחִיד עוֹשֶׂה,
phrases.english: Not everyone who wants to make himself a yachid may do so;
[nor may everyone make himself] a student;
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא repeating the strict view in another name
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a person may not decide on his own to act as a יחיד or a תלמיד.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: honors no, hardships yes
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the restriction to things that bring honor. For things that bring pain, like fasting, a person may take them on and is remembered for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: When is this said? For a matter of praise. But for a matter of pain, he may do so and is remembered for good, because it is not praise for him but pain for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל draws a line. He forbids taking on the honors of a scholar by yourself, but allows taking on its hardships.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that a person should not grab honor that is not his. But painful practices like fasting are not honor, so anyone may take them on. This states clearly the line behind רבי יוסי's reason in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (limits a rule)
A matter of pain or hardship

steps.whatToRemember: Taking on a scholar's honors by yourself is not allowed. Taking on a scholar's hardships, like fasting, is allowed and praised, since it is pain, not praise.
steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not fully reject the first opinion. He limits it to matters of honor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general guideline: extra strictness that brings suffering is not treated as showing off, but taking on honors is.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים: בְּדָבָר שֶׁל שֶׁבַח,
phrases.english: In what case is this said? In a matter of praise;
but in a matter of pain, he may do so,
and he is remembered for good,
for it is not praise for him,
but rather it is pain for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים: בְּדָבָר שֶׁל שֶׁבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's restriction to matters of honor
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The restriction applies only to matters of honor. A person may take on painful practices like fasting and is remembered for good.

steps.title: Finishing a fast, and fasting when you travel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a fast is completed even if the trouble passed. A traveller fasts if his new place fasts, and finishes his fast if his home place was fasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone was fasting because of a trouble and the trouble passed, or because of a sick person who got better. He still fasts and finishes the day. Someone goes from a place that is not fasting to a place that is fasting: he fasts with them. Someone goes from a place that is fasting to a place that is not fasting: he still fasts and finishes the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with practical rules about finishing a fast and about fasting while travelling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a fast has begun, it is not stopped just because its reason disappeared. When a person moves between places, he always ends up on the stricter side. He joins a fast where he arrives, and he does not drop the fast he began at home.

keyTerms.meaning: He fasts and completes the fast

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיָה מִתְעַנֶּה עַל הַצָּרָה וְעָבְרָה,
phrases.english: One who was fasting over a trouble, and it passed,
or over a sick person, and he was healed —
he fasts and completes the fast.
One who goes from a place where they are not fasting
to a place where they are fasting —
he fasts with them.
From a place where they are fasting to a place where they are not fasting —
he fasts and completes the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִי שֶׁהָיָה מִתְעַנֶּה עַל הַצָּרָה וְעָבְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who may take on a personal fast (steps 5-8) to practical rules for keeping a fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fast that was started is completed even if its reason ended. A traveller fasts with a fasting town, and completes a fast he started in his home town.

steps.title: If he forgot and ate during the fast
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if he ate by mistake, he should not appear full before the public or indulge himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he forgot and ate and drank, he should not show himself in front of the community, and he should not treat himself to luxuries.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a rule for someone who broke the fast by mistake: he should still act like a person who is fasting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating by mistake does not make the day a regular day for him. He must not look satisfied in public, and he should not go on to enjoy himself. The next step gives the source for this.

phrases.english: If he forgot, and ate and drank —
phrases.notes: He forgot that it was a fast day.

phrases.english: he should not show himself before the community,
and he should not treat himself to luxuries,

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁכַח וְאָכַל וְשָׁתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with another case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who ate by mistake on a fast day should not appear full in public or indulge himself.

steps.title: Source: יעקב told his sons not to look full
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves the rule from יעקב's words to his sons during the famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And יעקב said to his sons: Why do you show yourselves?" יעקב said to his sons: Do not show yourselves full, not in front of עשו and not in front of ישמעאל, so they will not be jealous of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to support the rule that you should not look full in front of people who are hungry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the famine, יעקב read "למה תתראו" as "why show yourselves full?" His concern was that hungry neighbors would become jealous. In the same way, a person who ate on a fast day should not look full in front of the fasting community.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (a פסוק is coming)

phrases.english: as it is said:
"And Yaakov said to his sons: Why do you show yourselves?"
Yaakov said to his sons:
Do not show yourselves when you are full,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּפְנֵי עֵשָׂו וְלֹא בִּפְנֵי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: not before Esav and not before Yishmael,
so that they will not be jealous of you.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב לְבָנָיו לָמָּה תִּתְרָאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the rule in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who ate should not appear full before the fasting public.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 42:1, read as יעקב warning his sons not to look full before hungry neighbors.
steps.whatToRemember: A fast is finished once begun. A traveller follows the stricter place. Someone who ate by mistake still should not look full in front of others who are hungry or fasting.

steps.title: יוסף's warning: no הלכה debates on the road
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains יוסף's words "אל תרגזו בדרך" as a warning not to get into הלכה discussions while travelling.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Do not quarrel on the way": רבי אלעזר said that יוסף told his brothers, Do not get busy with a matter of הלכה, or the road may turn against you.
steps.whatsHappening: Staying with the story of יוסף and his brothers, the גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's explanation of a פסוק about travelling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads יוסף's warning as advice not to get deep into הלכה on a journey. Doing so could cause trouble on the road. This sounds like it discourages Torah talk while travelling, and that sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not be agitated, do not quarrel

phrases.english: "Do not quarrel on the way":
phrases.notes: בראשית 45:24. יוסף says this as he sends his brothers home.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Yosef said to his brothers:
Do not get busy with a matter of halacha,
lest you stir up the road against yourselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל תִּרְגְּזוּ בַּדָּרֶךְ, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from יעקב's advice to his sons to יוסף's advice to his brothers. This is a new piece of travel advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Travellers should not get absorbed in הלכה discussions on the road.

steps.title: Challenge: scholars on the road must speak Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר from רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה, who says scholars walking without Torah talk deserve to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה said: Two Torah scholars walking on the road with no Torah talk between them deserve to be burned. As it says: "As they were walking and talking, behold a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them." They were saved only because they were talking Torah. Without that talk, they would have deserved to be burned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's teaching. Another אמורא holds that Torah talk on the road is required, not something to avoid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה learns from אליהו and אלישע: the fire separated them but did not hurt them, because they were speaking Torah. So Torah talk protects travellers. This seems to directly contradict רבי אלעזר's warning against discussing הלכה on the road.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is that there was

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this proves רבי אלעזר wrong. The גמרא is only raising the contradiction here, and the answer comes next.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rabbi Ilai bar Berechya say:
Two Torah scholars who are walking on the road
and there are no words of Torah between them —
they deserve to be burned,
as it is said:
"And it was, as they were walking and talking,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:11. "They" are אליהו and אלישע.

phrases.english: and behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire
and they separated the two of them."
The reason is that there was talk;
phrases.notes: He means the fire did not hurt them because they were talking Torah.

phrases.english: but if there were no talk —
they would deserve to be burned!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעַאי בַּר בֶּרֶכְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי אלעזר's teaching from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that travellers should not get busy with הלכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה infers from אליהו and אלישע that Torah talk on the road protects scholars, and that silence makes them deserve burning. That conflicts with a warning against discussing הלכה while travelling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's coming distinction about what kind of Torah learning fits a journey.

steps.title: Reviewing is allowed on the road, deep analysis is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction: רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה means reviewing learned material, and רבי אלעזר means deep analysis.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. This one is about reviewing, and that one is about analyzing in depth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the last step by showing that each opinion is talking about a different kind of learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה, who says travelers must talk Torah, means simple review of material already learned. רבי אלעזר, who says not to get into הלכה talk on the road, means deep analysis, which can lead to arguments and distraction. So the two opinions do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
To review or repeat learning one already knows

steps.whatToRemember: On the road: review Torah, yes. Get into deep analysis and debate, no.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is about reviewing,
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה, who said travelers must speak words of Torah.

phrases.english: That one is about analyzing in depth.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — לְמִיגְרַס, הָא — לְעַיּוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא raised in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each statement is about a different kind of learning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed רבי אלעזר forbids Torah talk on the road while רבי אלעאי בר ברכיה requires it
steps.terutzMaskana: Review is required on the road, and in-depth analysis is to be avoided

steps.title: A ברייתא: no long strides, and reach town while it is light
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds two more pieces of יוסף's travel advice: do not take long strides, and enter the city while the sun is still up.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: Do not take long strides, and bring the sun into the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two more travel warnings from יוסף to his brothers. The next steps explain each warning one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Bring the sun into the city" means arrive while the sun is still shining, before nightfall. The ברייתא gives the rules without reasons, so the גמרא will supply a reason for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Bring the sun into the city; arrive before sunset

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Do not take long strides,
and bring the sun into the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: אַל תַּפְסִיעוּ פְּסִיעָה גַּסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more of יוסף's travel advice after the discussion of אל תרגזו בדרך
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Travelers should not take long strides and should arrive in town before dark

steps.title: Why not take long strides: it harms eyesight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a long stride takes away one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not take long strides, because the Master said: A long stride takes away one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first warning of the ברייתא by quoting a known teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long strides might get you there faster, but they cost a small piece of your eyesight each time. That damage is not worth the time saved.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said; introduces a known teaching
Eyesight; literally the light of the eyes

phrases.english: Do not take long strides —
as the Master said:
A long stride takes away
one five-hundredth
of a person's eyesight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל תַּפְסִיעוּ פְּסִיעָה גַּסָּה — דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the ברייתא in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A long stride damages one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight

steps.title: Why arrive by daylight: leave and enter with "כי טוב"
steps.stepSummary: The second warning matches רב יהודה quoting רב: a person should always set out and arrive in daylight, as the פסוק shows with יוסף's brothers leaving in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bring the sun into the city, as רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person should always leave with "it is good" and enter with "it is good," as it says, "The morning was light, and the men were sent away."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second warning of the ברייתא using a teaching of רב, which it backs up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "כי טוב" is the Torah's phrase about light on the first day of creation, so it stands for daylight. A traveler should leave after sunrise and enter a new place before sunset, when it is safe. The proof is that יוסף's brothers were sent away only once morning came.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is good"; here it stands for daylight
As it is stated; brings a פסוק as proof

phrases.english: And bring the sun into the city —
this follows what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.
As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
A person should always set out with "it is good"
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:4, where light is called "good." So this means: travel in daylight.

phrases.english: and enter with "it is good,"
as it is stated:
"The morning was light, and the men were sent away."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַכְנִיסוּ חַמָּה לָעִיר — כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the ברייתא in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler should leave and arrive only during daylight

steps.title: A traveler should eat no more than in a famine year
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quoting רבי חייא teaches that someone on the road should not eat more than he would in a year of famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רבי חייא: One who walks on the road should not eat more than in years of famine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another piece of travel advice, this one about how much to eat on a journey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A traveler should keep his meals small, like someone eating carefully during a famine. The rule comes without a reason, so the גמרא will ask for one next.

keyTerms.meaning: One who travels on the road

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
One who walks on the road —
should not eat more than in years of famine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא: הַמְהַלֵּךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another travel rule after the advice about walking and daylight
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler should eat only famine-sized portions

steps.title: What is the reason for eating little on the road?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a traveler should limit his food.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי חייא's rule. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question looking for a reason, not an attack on the rule. Knowing the reason will matter when the גמרא later asks what practical difference there is between the two answers.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a traveler should eat less

steps.title: Two reasons: the digestion, or saving food
steps.stepSummary: In בבל they said the reason is to protect the bowels. In ארץ ישראל they said it is so the food supply will last.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they explained: because of the bowels. In the West they say: because of the food supply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different reasons for the rule, one from the scholars in בבל and one from the scholars in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars in בבל say a full stomach can be harmed by the effort of traveling, so a traveler should eat less for his health. The scholars in ארץ ישראל say a traveler who eats too much may run out of food before the trip ends, so he must ration it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Here they explained:
because of the bowels.
In the West they say:
because of the food supply.
phrases.notes: He means that if you eat too much now, your food may not last the whole trip.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא תַּרְגִּימוּ: מִשּׁוּם מַעְיָינָא. בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרִי: מִשּׁוּם מְזוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either to protect the digestion (בבל) or to make the food supply last (ארץ ישראל)

steps.title: What difference is there between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two reasons and begins its answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them? There is a difference between them,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks in which case the two reasons would lead to a different result. It starts to answer, and the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons lead to the same basic rule, so the גמרא looks for a case where only one reason applies. The words "איכא בינייהו" open the answer, which comes right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?
There is a difference between them; introduces the answer

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. "איכא בינייהו" only opens the answer, and the actual case that shows the difference comes next.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
There is a difference between them,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ? אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two reasons in step 20 differ in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons lead to different results
